definition: Blood sugar level – measures how much sugar (glucose) is in your blood after fasting.
Blood sugar measured after not eating for 8-12 hours.
Glycated hemoglobin – shows your average blood sugar over the past 2-3 months.
Total cholesterol level in your blood. High levels increase heart disease risk.
Good cholesterol – higher is better; helps remove bad cholesterol from arteries.
Bad cholesterol – high levels cause plaque buildup in arteries.
A type of fat in the blood. High levels raise heart disease risk.
Protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body.
Percentage of blood volume made up of red blood cells.
White blood cell count – part of the immune system that fights infections.
Red blood cell count – cells that carry oxygen from lungs to the body.
Number of platelets in blood – helps blood clot properly.
Waste product filtered by kidneys. High levels may indicate kidney problems.
BUN – measures kidney function by checking urea nitrogen in blood.
Waste product from digesting purine-rich foods. High levels can cause gout.
ALT – a liver enzyme. High levels can indicate liver damage or disease.
AST – a liver enzyme found in heart and liver. Elevated levels suggest tissue damage.
ALP – enzyme found in liver and bones. Elevated in liver or bone disease.
Yellow pigment from red blood cell breakdown. High levels cause jaundice.
Measures albumin and globulin proteins in blood. Indicates liver/kidney health.
Protein made by the liver. Low levels may indicate liver or kidney disease.
Mineral important for bones, muscles, and nerves.
Electrolyte that helps maintain fluid balance and nerve function.
Electrolyte essential for heart, muscle, and nerve cell function.
Thyroid Stimulating Hormone – controls thyroid gland activity.
Triiodothyronine – active thyroid hormone that regulates metabolism.
Thyroxine – thyroid hormone. Abnormal levels indicate thyroid disease.
Essential vitamin for bone health and immune function.
Vitamin needed for nerve function and red blood cell formation.
Mineral needed for hemoglobin production and oxygen transport.
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate – indicates inflammation in the body.
C-reactive protein – marker of inflammation or infection.
